source_text:
Σὺ τὸν ἄρτον ἐζύμωσας, ἀλλ' ἡ Σιὼν
δεῖπνον ἀνέδειξε. Σὺ τὸν μόσχον ἐπὶ τῆς φάτνης ἔθρεψας, ἀλλ' ἡ Σιὼν εἰς τὸν βωμὸν
ἀνήγαγε. Σὺ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐν τοῖς σπαρ γάνοις ἔκρυψας, αὕτη δὲ τῷ Θωμᾷ τὴν
πλευρὰν βουληθέντι ψηλαφῆσαι ἐγύμνωσε. Σὺ παρθένον ἔχεις τίκτουσαν
κεκλεισμένων τῶν ὀργάνων τῆς φύσεως, αὕτη παστάδα κεκλεισμένων τῶν θυρῶν
ἔνδον τὸν νυμφίον δεχομένην καὶ ἔχουσαν.
thought_title: Bethlehem's hidden mysteries versus Zion's open fulfillment
orientation: Hesychius continues his comparison between Bethlehem, where Christ's mysteries were hidden, and Zion, where they are now revealed and fulfilled.
pass_a_gloss: You leavened the bread, but Zion showed forth a supper. You nourished the calf upon the manger, but Zion led [it] up to the altar. You hid Jesus in the swaddling clothes, but this [one] bared the side to Thomas, [who] wished to touch [it]. You have a virgin giving birth while the organs of nature were closed, but this [one] [has] a bridal chamber receiving the bridegroom within while the doors were closed, and holding [him].

choices.why: ἀναδείκνυμι means to display or show forth publicly, contrasting with the hidden leavening in Bethlehem; 'supper' keeps the eucharistic resonance without over-translating.
The calf is the fatted calf, a sacrificial image; 'calf' is literal and preserves the animal reference.
γυμνόω means to make bare or naked; 'bared' is literal and vivid for exposing Christ's side to Thomas.
Glossary term; the bridal chamber is the place where the bridegroom is received within closed doors, contrasting with Bethlehem's closed womb.
Literal rendering of the physiological term; 'organs of nature' preserves the anatomical sense of the closed womb.

pass_b_english: You leavened the bread, but Zion displayed a supper. You nourished the calf at the manger, but Zion led it up to the altar. You hid Jesus in swaddling clothes, but she bared his side to Thomas when he wished to touch it. You have a virgin giving birth while the organs of nature remained closed; she has a bridal chamber that, while the doors were closed, receives the bridegroom within and holds him.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'Bethlehem' as English for Βηθλεέμ; 'You' obscures the contrast with Zion.
last_rejected.fix: Bethlehem leavened the bread, but Zion displayed a supper.
last_rejected.ruling: Σύ means 'you'; no Βηθλεέμ in source. 'You' correctly renders the pronoun contrast with ἡ Σιών.

last_rejected.ruling: ὄργανα includes 'organs' in LSJ; τῶν ὀργάνων τῆς φύσεως = 'organs of nature,' standard rendering.

last_rejected.quote: she bared his side to Thomas
last_rejected.source_quote: αὕτη δὲ τῷ Θωμᾷ τὴν πλευρὰν βουληθέντι ψηλαφῆσαι ἐγύμνωσε
last_rejected.why: English 'she' = Zion, but subject of ἐγύμνωσε is grammatically ambiguous; context suggests Christ (or the Church) bared his side, yet 'she' misleads.
last_rejected.fix: Zion bared his side to Thomas when he wished to touch it
last_rejected.ruling: αὕτη δὲ grammatically refers to Zion (fem.); she is subject throughout. 'She' is correct, not misleading.

problems.quote: she has a bridal chamber that receives the bridegroom within closed doors
problems.why: Bridal chamber (nymphon) for Christ's wounded side? Or upper room? Mixed metaphor.
problems.fix: Footnote: nymphon may mean tomb or upper room; clarify typology.

edits.old: she has a bridal chamber that receives the bridegroom within closed doors and holds him.
edits.new: she has a bridal chamber that, while the doors were closed, receives the bridegroom within and holds him.

fixed: The English already says the same thing as the source; the problem is interpretive, not a mistranslation. The wording 'within closed doors' was slightly adjusted to match the source's 'while the doors were closed' more closely.
